messages:
felix (newhire): hey team, first day and hitting a weird one. i can connect to WireGuard and the tunnel shows as up, but I can't reach our internal S3-compatible endpoint `dev-s3.internal` from my phone hotspot (macbook tether). works fine on home wifi. any ideas? :wave:

rachel: welcome felix! quick Q: when you say "phone hotspot" is that iPhone tethering or android? some carriers do CGNAT which breaks certain routes. also paste `ip route` and `dig dev-s3.internal` output.

felix (newhire): android hotspot. `ip route` shows default via 172.20.10.1 dev en0 and `10.100.0.0/16 via 10.11.11.1 dev utun0`. `dig dev-s3.internal` -> 10.100.2.12. wg handshake is recent.

 tom: so DNS resolves to private IP but can you `traceroute 10.100.2.12` and `curl -v http://10.100.2.12:9000/`? that'll show if packets leave your phone network and make it to our VPC.

felix (newhire): `traceroute`: only goes one hop to 100.64.0.1 then stops (looks like CGNAT). `curl` times out.

netops: CGNAT at carrier likely. Mobile hotspots can hide your real source IP so our NGW/NAT rules might drop the connection because the source port mapping doesn't match expected ranges. Two quick ways to test: 1) tether a different network (office wired or home) to see if it passes, 2) use the bastion SSH tunnel `ssh -L 9000:dev-s3.internal:9000 ec2-user@bastion-us-east-1` from your laptop and see if local port forwards work (this bypasses your carrier NAT for egress to VPC).

felix (newhire): tried office wired (works), ssh -L also works from hotspot — so definitely carrier NAT.

rachel: glad you found workaround. long-term we need to document hotspot caveat. also, for security we normally only allow our office/public egress ranges to talk to dev-s3. mobile CGNAT creates ephemeral source IP/port pairs which our SG and firewall may treat as invalid. tom, can you confirm if we have a proxy or NAT exception we want to offer for on-call mobile access?

 tom: we do have a documented on-call SSH bastion pattern for mobile users — basically instruct them to use the bastion tunnel for admin ops. For app traffic we avoid opening S3 endpoints publicly. We can consider a temporary relay or port-forwards for support sessions, but not a permanent public rule.

infra-bot: Ticket NET-9019 created: "onboard note: mobile hotspot CGNAT causes VPC reachability failures; document bastion-tunnel workaround" assigned to eng-infra.

steph: addition: we should add a short check in the onboarding smoke tests: if client detected behind CGNAT (traceroute sees RFC6598 100.64.0.0/10), surface a message recommending bastion tunnel and link to troubleshooting doc. felix, would you be willing to add the repro steps you ran to a tiny PR in /docs/onboarding/network.md? it helps new hires who try to use hotspots.

felix (newhire): sure thing — i'll open a PR with the traceroute output + steps (ssh -L example) and note that company wifi and home work but mobile hotspots may not. thanks for the quick help everyone! :relieved:

rachel: one more thing — tagging this thread for the on-call handbook so future on-call rotations include the bastion-tunnel pattern for mobile. :white_check_mark:

netops: leaving a note: if someone absolutely needs live app traffic from a mobile network we can provision a temporary NAT gateway and add the phone's public IP, but that's an ops-only flow (needs ticket + justification). prefer bastion tunnel.

infra-bot: ENGINF-2321 created: "add onboarding smoke test to detect CGNAT + doc update" linked to NET-9019.
